messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: PAGER fired for service=redwood-edge-lb region=eu-west-1 severity=critical — 2265432100

pagerduty: 🚨 Incident triggered: redwood-edge-lb — TLS handshake errors + target health failing (auto-escalation in 5m)

ravi (oncall): Acked. I'm jumping on this. Looking at ALB health checks now.

marie (sre): I see increased 502/504 from the EU edge in Grafana, plus TLS alert from edge-prober.

chao (netops): Confirmed: backend targets showing Unhealthy in eu-west-1 and some 502s in us-west-2. Could be certificate mismatch or backend process crash.

ravi (oncall): Running quick curl against /health on a few targets:
```
curl -v https://backend-eu-1.internal/health
* TLS 1.3 handshake failed: handshake timeout
* Connection timed out
```

marie (sre): Also seeing SNI mismatch errors in the ALB logs: `tls_alert: unexpected_message` from connections to targets.

sam (platform): Deploybot? Any recent cert rotations or LB config changes tonight?

karen (support): Customer tickets started coming in ~5m ago complaining models timing out. Some enterprise customers in EU reporting elevated latency.

ravi (oncall): I'm failing traffic away from the unhealthy target group to the standby pool in the same region. Will update routing weight. Executing runbook step 3.

incident-bot: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/lb-unhealthy — next step: failover to backup target group (manual).

marie (sre): +1 on failover. Also reduce connection draining timeout to speed replacement while we investigate root cause.

chao (netops): Checking DNS — cname and ALIAS look fine; TTL is 60s for edge records. No recent Route53 changes in last 24h.

ravi (oncall): Failover complete for eu-west-1 -> standby-target-group-eu-1. Health checks are improving for the new targets. Monitoring.

pagerduty: Escalation: if errors persist, PD will escalate to SEV-2 managers in 10 minutes.

sam (platform): I'm pushing a temporary autoscaling policy bump for standby pool to absorb traffic while we validate targets.

marie (sre): Looking at container logs from one of the failed targets — stack traces show OpenSSL handshake errors when initializing TLS context: `error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number`. Might be a TLS config regression in the app.

chao (netops): If app is binding to plaintext on the TLS port accidentally, that would explain TLS handshake failures. Any recent config pushes?

ravi (oncall): @sam any deployment to model-serving in the last hour?

sam (platform): There was a config-only rollout to change JVM TLS policies 40m ago in canary, but it was stalled. I will check if it reached prod.

sam (platform): Confirmed — a config flag toggled `jdk.tls.client.protocols` and it leaked to one AZ due to a rolling flag bug. Rolling it back now.

marie (sre): Nice catch. Once rollback finishes we should see TLS handshakes normalize. Keep the standby pool in front until we confirm 10m of stable health.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: acknowledged by ravi — assigned to SRE. Escalation suspended.

karen (support): Updating customers: "We experienced degraded performance in EU region due to a TLS configuration regression. Traffic has been rerouted and mitigation is in progress. We'll follow up when fully resolved."

ravi (oncall): Rollback applied across AZs. I'm running a health sweep: `for ip in $(cat targets.txt); do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://$ip/health; done` — most returning 200 now.

marie (sre): Grafana metrics show error rate dropping back to baseline over the last 3m. Latency also improving.

chao (netops): Confirmed ALB target state: healthy -> 99% in eu-west-1. No DNS changes required.

ravi (oncall): Taking incident -> monitoring state. Will remain in thread for 30m for handoff. Please don't trigger PD until we have 10m stable.

pagerduty: Incident marked as mitigated by ravi. Auto-escalation disabled.

sam (platform): Follow-ups: add guardrail to prevent rolling flag from affecting multiple AZs, add test to release pipeline to validate TLS handshake after config flips.

marie (sre): Postmortem owner volunteers? I can take initial writeup. Action items: root cause = config flag leak -> TLS mismatch; mitigations = failover + rollback; follow-ups = release guardrails + add canary verification for TLS.

karen (support): I'll send an external incident update to impacted customers after we lock down postmortem drafts.

ravi (oncall): Handoff to night oncall in 30m. Leaving thread open until then. Thanks all :heart:
